message.content:
# Percentage Composition in Chemistry

## What It Is

Percentage composition tells you **how much of each element (by mass) is present in a compound**, expressed as a percentage. It answers the question: *"If I had 100 g of this compound, how many grams would each element contribute?"*

## The Formula

$$\% \text{ Composition of an element} = \frac{\text{Mass of that element in 1 mole of compound}}{\text{Molar mass of the compound}} \times 100$$

### Step-by-Step (Example: H₂O)

| Step | What You Do | Detail |
|------|-------------|--------|
| 1 | Write the formula | H₂O |
| 2 | Find atomic masses | H = 1, O = 16 |
| 3 | Calculate total mass per element | H: 2×1 = 2 g; O: 1×16 = 16 g |
| 4 | Find molar mass of compound | 2 + 16 = 18 g |
| 5 | Divide each element's mass by total | H: 2/18; O: 16/18 |
| 6 | Multiply by 100 | H: **11.1%**; O: **88.9%** |

## Why It Matters for NMDCAT

- Used to **determine empirical formulas** (you'll be given % by mass → convert to moles → find simplest ratio).
- Helps verify molecular formulas.
- Appears in stoichiometry-based MCQs.

## Common Traps

- Don't confuse **% by mass** with **% by atoms** (mole fraction).
- Always use the **molar mass of the entire compound** as the denominator, not just one element.

---

```
│          PERCENTAGE COMPOSITION — CHUNKMAP              │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                                                         │
│  G — GOAL                                              │
│  "Find mass % of each element in a compound"           │
│                                                         │
│  R — RELATION                                          │
│  Feeds into → Empirical Formula → Molecular Formula    │
│  Connects → Atomic mass table, Molar mass, Stoich.     │
│                                                         │
│  I — INPUT (what you need before starting)             │
│  • Correct molecular formula                           │
│  • Atomic masses of all elements present               │
│                                                         │
│  N — NUMBER (the formula to memorize)                  │
│  % = (mass of element / molar mass of compound) × 100  │
│  Always: sum of all % = 100 (check your work)          │
│                                                         │
│  D — DISTINCTION (don't mix up)                        │
│  • % by mass ≠ mole fraction ≠ atomic ratio            │
│  • Denominator = WHOLE compound, not one element        │
│  • Use molar mass (g/mol), not atomic mass alone       │
│                                                         │
│  E — EXAMPLE (anchor memory)                           │
│  H₂O → H: 11.1%, O: 88.9%                             │
│  CO₂ → C: 27.3%, O: 72.7%                             │
│  NaCl → Na: 39.3%, Cl: 60.7%                          │
│                                                         │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```
